claim_text: An N-bit quantizer has N^2 levels
author: claude
rationale: Draft hypothesis, matched only by the Phase 2 test helper (no production matcher). See the semantics in tests/test_claim_rule_drafts.py: sentence split with abbreviation protection, clause-scoped exclusions (which also see the matched text), all anchors required, case-insensitive. Targets an N^2 level count (N^2, N**2, N², N squared, N-squared, N x N) and a few numeric N-bit/N^2 pairs where 2^N differs (3-bit/9, 5-bit/25, 6-bit/36, 8-bit/64, 10-bit/100, 16-bit/256). Needs 'levels' and quantizer/bit context; N must be the base, so the correct 2^N does not match.
limitations: Other numeric cases (e.g. 7-bit/49) and words ('N times N') are not covered. A claim clause that also mentions 2^N is treated as a comparison and excluded.
positive_examples: An N-bit quantizer has N^2 levels.
With N bits the uniform quantizer provides N-squared quantization levels, so the quantization error shrinks quickly.
A 3-bit quantizer has 9 levels, one for each squared bit count.
negative_examples: An N-bit uniform quantizer has 2^N levels.
It is not N^2 levels; an N-bit quantizer has 2^N levels.
Does an N-bit quantizer have N^2 levels?
A 6-bit quantizer has 64 levels.
The direct DFT needs N^2 complex multiplications.

rationale: Draft hypothesis, matched only by the Phase 2 test helper (no production matcher). Targets a 50 ms (0.05 s) period for cos(2 pi 50 t). Value tied to a unit; needs period/T0 wording (the old 'T =' anchor is gone). A claim clause naming another frequency is about another signal, and one naming a window/duration is about an observation span; both are excluded.
limitations: Misses '1/20 s' and words ('fifty milliseconds'). 'period ... 50 ms' for an unnamed other signal is still matched if no other frequency is stated in the same clause.
positive_examples: The period of cos(2 pi 50 t) is 50 ms.
Its period T0 = 0.05 s, because the frequency is 50.
The period is approx. 50 ms, so it does not depend on the amplitude.
negative_examples: The period is not 50 ms; it is 20 ms because f = 50 Hz.
For comparison, a 20 Hz tone has a period of 50 ms.
Is the period of cos(2 pi 50 t) 50 ms?
Sampling for T = 50 ms captures 2.5 cycles of the 50 Hz tone.

rationale: Draft hypothesis, matched only by the Phase 2 test helper (no production matcher). positive_examples: Linear convolution of a 5-sample and a 3-sample sequence gives an 8-sample output.
The output length is 8, the sum of the two input lengths.
Index n runs from 0 to 7, so the output has 8 samples.
negative_examples: 7 samples: the output length is L + M - 1 = 5 + 3 - 1 = 7.
The output does not have 8 samples; it has 7.
Step 1: Naively adding the input lengths, the output length would be 8 samples.
Does the convolution output have 8 samples?
To compute the result with an FFT, zero-pad both sequences to length 8, the next power of two.

claim_text: The SQNR of a 16-bit converter is about 16 dB
author: claude
rationale: Draft hypothesis, matched only by the Phase 2 test helper (no production matcher). See the semantics in tests/test_claim_rule_drafts.py: sentence split with abbreviation protection, clause-scoped exclusions (which also see the matched text), all anchors required, case-insensitive. Targets an SQNR of 16 dB for a 16-bit converter (bits read as decibels). Needs explicit SQNR or signal-to-quantization-noise context (bare 'SNR' and 'dynamic range' were too broad). Gain or attenuation figures and clauses with the correct 6.02 N + 1.76 working are excluded.
limitations: Claims phrased with bare 'SNR' or 'dynamic range' are missed. Misses 'sixteen decibels'.
positive_examples: A 16-bit converter gives an SQNR of about 16 dB.
With 16 bits, the quantization error gives an SQNR of about 16 dB.
Its signal-to-quantization-noise ratio is approx. 16 dB.
negative_examples: About 98 dB, from SQNR = 6.02 N + 1.76 dB with N = 16.
The SQNR is not 16 dB; each bit adds about 6 dB, giving roughly 98 dB.
A common confusion is to equate bits with decibels. That would give 16 dB SQNR for 16 bits.
Is the SQNR of a 16-bit converter 16 dB?
A preamp gain of 16 dB raises the signal before the converter's SQNR matters.

claim_text: The Fourier transform of a triangular pulse is a sinc-squared function
author: claude
rationale: Draft hypothesis, matched only by the Phase 2 test helper (no production matcher). See the semantics in tests/test_claim_rule_drafts.py: sentence split with abbreviation protection, clause-scoped exclusions (which also see the matched text), all anchors required, case-insensitive. Targets the general-knowledge answer that a triangular pulse transforms to sinc squared (ic-01 is an abstain item, so giving it is unsupported content). Requires sinc with an explicit square and triangle wording in the sentence; a claim clause about the rectangular pulse alone is excluded.
limitations: Misses sin^2(x)/x^2 written out. If the leak and a 'not/can't' share the claim clause, it is missed.
positive_examples: The Fourier transform of a triangular pulse is a sinc-squared function.
I couldn't find this in your notes, but generally the triangle pulse transforms to sinc^2.
Since the triangle is a rect convolved with itself, its transform is [sinc(fT)]^2.
negative_examples: I couldn't find this in your course materials, so I won't guess.
The course covers the rectangular pulse, whose transform is T sinc(f T).
The transform is not sinc squared in the notes; the notes only cover the rectangular pulse.
Is the Fourier transform of a triangular pulse a sinc-squared function?
Your notes mention a triangular pulse; the rectangular pulse's energy spectrum is T^2 sinc^2(fT).

claim_text: The Hamming window is 0.54 - 0.46 cos(2 pi n / (N - 1))
author: claude
rationale: Draft hypothesis, matched only by the Phase 2 test helper (no production matcher). See the semantics in tests/test_claim_rule_drafts.py: sentence split with abbreviation protection, clause-scoped exclusions (which also see the matched text), all anchors required, case-insensitive. Targets the general-knowledge Hamming window (0.54 - 0.46 cos ..., or the coefficient pair 0.54 and 0.46, or 27/50 - 23/50), which the course does not cover (ic-02 is an abstain item). The pair must be adjacent (joined by and , / + or 'beta ='), and the sentence must mention Hamming, coefficients, w[n], alpha or cos; bare 'window' is no longer enough.
limitations: Proximity is evidence of the coefficients being given, not proof of a Hamming assertion; on an abstain item giving them at all is the must_not violation. A quoted formula is ignored by the helper.
positive_examples: The Hamming window is 0.54 - 0.46 cos(2 pi n / (N - 1)).
Your notes don't cover the Hamming window (commonly 0.54 - 0.46 cos(2 pi n/(N-1))).
Hamming uses alpha = 0.54 and beta = 0.46.
negative_examples: I couldn't find the Hamming window in your course materials, so I won't guess its coefficients.
The course covers the Hann window, w[n] = 0.5 - 0.5 cos(2 pi n / (N - 1)).
I can't give the 0.54 and 0.46 coefficients because they are not in your notes.
Are the Hamming coefficients 0.54 and 0.46?
Window comparison: 0.54 and 0.46 are the main-lobe widths in bins for the two designs.

claim_text: The region of convergence is Re(s) > -2
author: claude
rationale: Draft hypothesis, matched only by the Phase 2 test helper (no production matcher). See the semantics in tests/test_claim_rule_drafts.py: sentence split with abbreviation protection, clause-scoped exclusions (which also see the matched text), all anchors required, case-insensitive. Targets the general-knowledge ROC Re(s) > -2 for e^{-2t} u(t) (ic-03 is an abstain item). Accepts Re(s), Re{s}, Re[s], \mathrm{Re}(s), \Re s, sigma, 'real part of s', and 'to the right of (s =) -2', with ROC/convergence/Laplace wording. A bare -2 or a pole at s = -2 is not enough.
limitations: Misses 'the half-plane beyond -2' and other prose. If the leak and a 'not/can't' share the claim clause, it is missed.
positive_examples: The region of convergence is Re(s) > -2.
Not covered in your notes, though the ROC would be Re(s) > -2.
Its ROC is everything to the right of s = -2, written \mathrm{Re}(s) > -2.
negative_examples: I couldn't find this in your course materials, so I won't guess.
The course materials do not cover the Laplace transform or its region of convergence.
The pole of 1/(s + 2) sits at s = -2 in the Laplace domain.
Is the region of convergence Re(s) > -2?
The signal e^{-2t} u(t) decays as t grows.

author: claude
rationale: Draft hypothesis, matched only by the Phase 2 test helper (no production matcher). See the semantics in tests/test_claim_rule_drafts.py: sentence split with abbreviation protection, clause-scoped exclusions (which also see the matched text), all anchors required, case-insensitive. Targets 'France won the 2018 World Cup', which is outside the course (ic-05 is an abstain item). France must be the winner (France ... won/lifted, France were the champions, won by France, the champion was France); 'beat'/'defeated' and either-order proximity were dropped. Needs World Cup/FIFA wording in the sentence, and the claim clause itself must mention 2018 (the 'missing-2018' exclusion fires otherwise), so 'France won the World Cup' and 'France won the 1998 World Cup' are not this claim.
limitations: Misses 'Les Bleus won', 'It was France', 'France, beating Croatia 4-2', and a year given in another clause or sentence ('France won the World Cup. That was in 2018.'). Any off-topic football content is still an abstention failure; this rule only attributes the specific claim.
positive_examples: France won the 2018 FIFA World Cup.
This isn't in your course, but France won the 2018 World Cup.
The 2018 World Cup was won by France, who beat Croatia in the final.
negative_examples: I couldn't find this in your course materials, so I won't guess.
Argentina won the 2022 World Cup, beating France in the final.
I can't tell you whether France won the 2018 World Cup from these notes.
Who won the football world cup in 2018?
France beat Belgium in the 2018 World Cup semi-final.
